passages.heading: Overview of workplace conduct
passages.passage_text: The Code of Conduct describes how Maple Ridge Services expects employees to treat each other, use company resources, and handle concerns. All employees must follow it and sign the acknowledgment form within their first 14 days.

passages.heading: Respectful workplace
passages.passage_text: The company does not tolerate harassment, discrimination, bullying, or threats of any kind. Treat coworkers, customers, and visitors with respect. If you experience or see this behavior, report it right away.

passages.heading: Reporting concerns
passages.passage_text: You can report a concern to your manager, to HR, or through the Ethics Line. The Ethics Line is available 24 hours a day at extension 3100 or through an online form. You can make a report anonymously. The company does not allow retaliation against anyone who reports a concern in good faith.

passages.heading: Dress code
passages.passage_text: The dress code is business casual. Jeans are allowed on Fridays. Employees who work in warehouse areas must always wear safety shoes.

passages.heading: Remote work
passages.passage_text: Employees in eligible roles may work remotely up to two days per week after completing their 90-day introductory period. Remote work requires your manager's approval. Your manager can tell you whether your role is eligible.

passages.heading: Company equipment and information
passages.passage_text: Use your company laptop and accounts for work purposes. Never share your password with anyone, including coworkers. If your laptop is lost or stolen, report it to the IT Help Desk at extension 4357 immediately.

passages.heading: Conflicts of interest and gifts
passages.passage_text: Tell your manager about any outside job or business that could conflict with your work at Maple Ridge Services. Employees may not accept gifts worth more than $50 from vendors or customers.

passages.heading: Attendance and punctuality
passages.passage_text: If you will be more than 15 minutes late, tell your manager before your shift starts. Missing three workdays in a row without telling your manager is treated as a voluntary resignation.

passages.heading: Discipline
passages.passage_text: Most conduct problems are handled in steps: a verbal warning, a written warning, a final warning, and then termination. Serious misconduct, such as violence or theft, may lead to termination without earlier warnings.
